sites.tag_type: short epitope, ALFA 15 aa, GS linkers (~17-23 aa total insert)
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Electrophysiology: tag demonstrated not to affect electrophysiological properties of the channel (DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606). Surface expression: confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy in HEK293T cells (PMC7704534). Processing and function: HA tag in S1–S2 loop does not interfere with processing and function (PMC3861077, citing Akhavan et al. 2003).
sites.rationale: The ledger line from DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606 explicitly names T443 and E444 as the junction. Python lookup confirms seq[443]='T' and seq[444]='E', matching the paper exactly. The junction lies within the extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology: 430–453), 14 residues from TM1 end (429) and 10 residues from TM2 start (454), both well above the >=3 aa minimum. The same paper confirms electrophysiological function is preserved; multiple independent groups (PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC7704534, PMC13182972) have used HA-tagged hERG in this same loop with confirmed surface expression and unperturbed function. Ranked first due to highest validation level (surface_and_function) and explicit residue-level citation. A 9 aa HA tag with flanking 4 aa linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE, 17 aa total) was inserted between T443 and E444 in the extracellular S1–S2 loop of full-length KCNH2 (hERG1a) by inverse PCR in a stable HEK293 cell line. The tag was demonstrated not to affect electrophysiological properties of the channel. Surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry and confocal microscopy across multiple independent studies using HA-tagged hERG constructs in the same S1–S2 loop. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: A previously published 34 9 amino acid HA tag with surrounding 4 amino acid linkers (NSEHYPYDVPDYAVTFE) was inserted between amino acids T443 and E444 (in the extracellular region between the S1 and S2 helices) by inverse PCR 35 (Table S1).

literature_notes: Both validated sites lie in the same extracellular S1–S2 loop (topology 430–453) of KCNH2. All other ledger lines (PMC3861077, PMC3877390, PMC7704534, PMC13182972) describe HA-tagged hERG in the S1–S2 loop without specifying the exact residue junction; they corroborate the general loop tolerance but do not independently pin a third residue-level site and so are cited as supporting evidence for site 1 rather than as separate sites. No ledger evidence supports any other extracellular loop (S3–S4 loop: 501; turret/S5–S6 loop: 571–638) with a tag insertion in full-length membrane-anchored KCNH2.

literature_rejected.reason: These ledger lines confirm the S1–S2 loop is tolerant of HA tags and confirm surface expression and/or function, but do not state the exact residue junction. They are used as corroborating evidence for the T443/E444 site (which is explicitly pinned by DOI:10.1101/2020.02.17.952606) rather than as independent sites, because no distinct residue number can be extracted to define a separate insert_after_residue.
